summary: In a US copyright case brought by music publishers Universal Music Group, Concord and ABKCO, Anthropic expert Olivia Chen submitted a declaration on how often Claude might reproduce song lyrics. A footnote cited an American Statistician article in support of her rare-event sampling discussion. At a 13 May 2025 hearing, the publishers’ lawyer Matt Oppenheim challenged the title and authors as belonging to an article that did not exist, and Magistrate Judge Susan van Keulen ordered Anthropic to explain. In a 15 May declaration, Anthropic lawyer Ivana Dukanovic said a Latham & Watkins colleague had found a real article, then she asked Claude to format its citation using the correct link. Claude returned the right journal, year and link but the wrong title and authors; the legal team reviewed the article and corrected volume and page numbers yet missed those errors. Dukanovic also disclosed two other wording errors in the footnotes, apologised and said the firm had introduced additional review procedures.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The 13 May Reuters report identifies Chen’s expert declaration, the publishers’ challenge by Matt Oppenheim, Judge van Keulen’s order for an explanation and Anthropic attorney Sy Damle’s initial miscitation response. Dukanovic’s filed 15 May declaration supplies the source chain: a Latham & Watkins associate found the real McGrath and Burke article; Chen relied on it for her rare-event sampling opinion; Dukanovic provided its correct link to Claude for a formatted legal citation; the returned citation had wrong authors and title despite correct publication, year and link. She says the team reviewed the article and fixed page and volume numbers yet missed those errors, plus two other citation wording errors. The declaration records an apology, additional review procedures and preservation of related material. This corrects the early assertion of an entirely invented source and locates Claude use with counsel, not Chen. The source and human review account is counsel’s sworn statement; VIGIL has not independently adjudicated article support, intent or any later judicial ruling on the merits.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Dukanovic’s declaration describes a valid source and a narrow Claude formatting request, followed by invented bibliographic fields that passed human review into a court-facing expert declaration. The governance failure is the mismatch between the apparent precision of the generated citation and the fidelity required for formal legal reliance. The court challenge and counsel’s response expose and bound the error; the existence of a real linked article prevents characterising the supporting source itself as wholly fictitious. The current classification of epistemic reliance calibration is supported by the inaccurate formal citation. The declaration also gives more concrete evidence of a missed citation check, but does not by itself establish an independently mandated verification protocol for an additional failure class. It establishes no merits ruling or materialised deprivation of a party’s rights.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The correct source link and partial bibliographic accuracy allowed a wrong title and author list to survive a manual check and enter an expert declaration. This is a concrete source-fidelity problem at the point where generated formatting becomes formal evidence. The team’s reported review of the article did not include effective verification of all citation fields before submission; the subsequent challenge forced a documented correction and additional procedures.
